prompt: The point $(3, -2)$ is first reflected across the $y$-axis, and then the image is translated $4$ units up. Write the final coordinates in the form (x, y).
hint: Do the two moves in order, one at a time, and write down the point in between.

hints.text: Do the two moves in order, one at a time, and write down the point in between.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Practice on a friendlier point: reflect $(1, 0)$ across the $y$-axis to get $(-1, 0)$, then translate up $4$ to get $(-1, 4)$. Same two rules, applied in that order.
Reflecting across the $y$-axis (a vertical mirror) negates $x$: $(3, -2) \to (-3, -2)$.

explanation: Step 1 — reflect across the $y$-axis: the rule is $(x, y) \to (-x, y)$, so $(3, -2) \to (-3, -2)$.
Step 2 — translate $4$ units up: add $4$ to the $y$-coordinate, giving $(-3, -2 + 4)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Track each coordinate separately
steps: The $x$-coordinate is touched only by the reflection: $3 \to -3$.
The $y$-coordinate is touched only by the translation: $-2 \to 2$. Splitting the work this way keeps compositions from tangling.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The most common wrong answer is $(3, 2)$, from reflecting across the $x$-axis instead of the $y$-axis. The names feel backwards: reflecting across the $y$-AXIS changes the $x$-COORDINATE.
Anchor it with a picture: the $y$-axis is a vertical mirror, so the point hops left-right — and left-right is the $x$-coordinate's job.
